findings.problem: Ximen Bao, Xie Bian, and Marquis Wen are cited in the undated famine remonstrance. The reception has no era-year and cannot be approved as dated chronology.
findings.action: Retain unresolved:true and any one-sided floor already justified by the Chinese. Do not invent a Western year, close a 及/後/至是/是時 sequel, or import an encyclopedia date. Approval stays blocked until the passage names an era-year for this person’s own event.

units.zh: 駿境內嘗大饑，穀價踴貴，市長譚詳請出倉谷與百姓，秋收三倍征之。
units.en: A great famine once struck Jun's territory and grain prices soared. Market director Tan Xiang requested that grain from the granaries be issued to the people, then collected back at threefold after the autumn harvest.
units.literal: Within Jun’s borders there was once a great famine; grain prices leaped; market director Tan Xiang asked to release granary grain to the common people and after autumn harvest levy three times the amount in return.

units.zh: 從事陰據諫曰：「昔西門豹宰鄴，積之於人；
units.en: Aide Yin Ju remonstrated, saying, "In olden times Ximen Bao governed Ye and stored grain in the people;
units.literal: Aide Yin Ju remonstrated, saying, "In olden times Ximen Bao governed Ye and stored grain in the people;

units.zh: 解扁蒞東封之邑，計三倍。
units.en: When Xie Bian governed the eastern border towns, his accounts yielded a threefold profit.
units.literal: Xie Bian took charge of the eastern border town and reckoned a threefold return.

units.zh: 文侯以豹有罪而可賞，扁有功而可罰。
units.en: Marquis Wen judged that Bao had committed a punishable offense despite merit, while Bian had merit despite a punishable offense.
units.literal: Marquis Wen of Wei thought Bao guilty yet praiseworthy, and Bian meritorious yet punishable.

units.zh: 今詳欲因人之饑，以要三倍，反裘傷皮，未足喻之。」
units.en: Now Xiang wishes to exploit people’s hunger to demand threefold return—reversing the fur injures the skin is not enough to compare."
units.literal: Now Xiang wishes to exploit people’s hunger to demand threefold return—reversing the fur injures the skin is not enough to compare."

units.zh: 駿從之。
units.en: Zhang Jun approved and built the shrine.
units.literal: Jun followed this.

units.zh: 駿在位二十二年卒，時年四十，私諡曰文公，穆帝追諡曰忠成公。
units.en: Zhang Jun died at forty after twenty-two years in power; private posthumous title Wen; Emperor Mu later styled him Zhongcheng.
units.literal: Jun died in the twenty-second year of his reign at the age of forty; privately he was titled Duke Wen; Emperor Mu posthumously titled him Duke Zhongcheng.

units.zh: 駿子重華
units.en: Zhang Chonghua, Zhang Jun’s heir
units.literal: Son of Jun: Chonghua

units.zh: 在位十一年。
units.en: He ruled eleven years.
units.literal: He had occupied the position eleven years.

units.zh: 私諡曰昭公，後改曰桓公，穆帝賜諡曰敬烈。
units.en: Private posthumous titles changed to Huan; Emperor Mu named him Jinglie.
units.literal: Privately he was titled Duke Zhao, later changed to Duke Huan; Emperor Mu granted the posthumous title Reverent and Fierce.

units.zh: 子耀靈嗣。
units.en: His son Zhang Yaoling inherited.
units.literal: His son Yaoling succeeded.

units.zh: 祚篡立三年而亡。
units.en: Zhang Zuo’s three-year reign ended in blood.
units.literal: Zuo usurped and stood three years then perished.

units.zh: 耀靈弟玄靚
units.en: Zhang Xuanjing, younger brother of Zhang Yaoling
units.literal: Younger brother of Yaoling: Xuanjing

units.zh: =玄靚字元安。
units.en: Zhang Xuanjing, courtesy name Yuan’an.
units.literal: = Xuanjing, courtesy name Yuan’an.

units.zh: 在位九年。
units.en: Zhang Xuanjing had ruled nine years.
units.literal: He had occupied the position nine years.

units.zh: 私諡曰沖公，孝武帝賜諡曰敬悼公。
units.en: He was posthumously titled Jingdao.
units.literal: Privately he was titled Duke Chong; Emperor Xiaowu granted the posthumous title Reverent and Mourned.

units.zh: 玄靚叔天錫
units.en: Zhang Tianxi, Zhang Xuanjing’s uncle
units.literal: Uncle of Xuanjing: Tianxi

units.zh: 尋卒，年六十一。
units.en: He died at sixty-one.
units.literal: Soon he died at the age of sixty-one.

units.zh: 追贈金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: The court posthumously awarded golden-purple grand master.
units.literal: Posthumous gifts made him grand master with golden purple ribbon.

units.zh: 史評
units.en: Section: historians’ appraisal
units.literal: Historians’ appraisal

units.zh: 史臣曰：長河外區，流沙作紀，玉關懸險，金城負固，有苗攸竄，帝舜投而不羈；
units.en: They paint the Hexi corridor’s harsh geography and ancient tribes;
units.literal: The historians say: Beyond the long river lies an outer region; drifting sands mark its bounds; the Jade Pass hangs perilous; Metal City leans on strength—where the Miao fled, Emperor Shun drove them yet could not bind them;

units.zh: 渠搜是居，大禹即而方敘。
units.en: Yu the Great ordered the western wastes.
units.literal: the Qu sou dwell there, and Great Yu approached and then set them in order.

units.zh: 世逢多難，嬰五郡以誰何；
units.en: Through generations of crisis they armed five commanderies and dared any challenger to intervene.
units.literal: Meeting many hard generations, they girded five commanderies and defied all comers;

units.zh: 雖非久安之地，足為苟全之所乎！
units.en: Hexi was no paradise but a refuge.
units.literal: Though it was no land of long peace, was it not enough for a place to preserve life awhile!

units.zh: 周公保之而立功，士彥擁之布延世。
units.en: The Duke of Zhou guarded it and achieved merit; Shiyan upheld it and extended the line.
units.literal: The Duke of Zhou guarded it and achieved merit; Shiyan upheld it and prolonged the generations.

units.zh: 摯虞觀象，記洪災之不流；
units.en: Zhi Yu watched the stars and recorded that the great flood’s waters did not reach;
units.literal: Zhi Yu watched the stars and recorded that the great flood’s waters did not reach;

units.zh: 侯瑾覘泉，知霸者之斯在。
units.en: Hou Jin’s spring prophecy foretold Zhang power.
units.literal: Hou Jin peered at the spring and knew a hegemon would be there.

units.zh: 匪唯地勢，抑亦有天道歙！
units.en: Heaven as well as earth favored the west.
units.literal: Not only terrain—was there not also Heaven’s way!

units.zh: 茂、駿、重華資忠踵武，崎嶇僻陋，無忘本朝，故能西控諸戎，東攘巨猾，綰累葉之珪組，賦絕域之琛賨，振曜遐荒，良由杖順之效矣。
units.en: The good early Zhangs held Jin’s mandate in the wilds and prospered.
units.literal: Mao, Jun, and Chonghua relied on loyalty and followed in martial footsteps; on cragged remote ground they did not forget the capital court; therefore they could control the various Rong to the west, brush aside great villains to the east, thread generation after generation of jade seals and silken cords, and levy treasure from the farthest lands—shaking brilliance across the wastes—truly the effect of wielding the righteous cause.

units.zh: 祚以卑孽，陰傾塚嗣，播有茨于彤管，擬宸居於黑山，丁琪以切諫遇誅夷，王鸞以讜言嬰顯戮，境內雲據，仇其竊名，卒致梟懸，自然之理也。
units.en: Zhang Zuo’s incest and usurpation brought a natural fall.
units.literal: Zuo, base-born, secretly overturned the heir, spread “tares on the wall” in the crimson tube, modeled the imperial seat on Black Mountain—Ding Qi met execution for blunt remonstrance, Wang Luan suffered clear execution for candid words—cloudlike factions within the borders hated his stolen name, until at last his head hung displayed—principle of nature.

units.zh: 純嘏微弱，竟亡其眾。
units.en: Zhang Tianxi’s weakness lost the army and state.
units.literal: Chungu being feeble, in the end he lost his hosts.

units.zh: 奉身魏闕，齒跡朝流，再襲銀黃，祖德之延慶矣。
units.en: Zhang Tianxi ended his days a Jin official, still honored as Zhang Gui’s heir.
units.literal: Offering himself to the Weique, treading in the tracks of court currents, twice donning silver and gold—extension of ancestral virtue’s blessing.

units.zh: 贊曰：三象構氛，九土瓜分。
units.en: The eulogy opens on cosmic chaos and partition.
units.literal: The encomium says: Three luminaries built miasma; the nine provinces were carved like a melon.
